units.title: Free before 9: bike, bookcase, tubs (11F)
units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Posting early because the van comes at nine. We can't fit everything, so free to anyone: R.'s old bike (needs a back tyre), a white bookcase (one shelf wobbles), and a big box of plastic tubs with lids. Knock on 11F before nine or I'll leave them by the lift on 11 with a note. Sorry about the noise this morning.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: I will take the tubs for the shop if nobody wants them, they are perfect for the loose sweets. I can carry the bookcase down for you too, the lift is working this morning. The van can use my loading space at the front, I have no delivery until eleven. H

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: There is a removal lorry across both disabled bays and half the access road. I appreciate people have to move, but the bays are marked, and the bin wagon comes on Thursdays at ten, and if it can't get round it will not come back, as I have explained on this board more than once. Good luck to the family all the same.

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Soraya, I watched R. learn to ride that bicycle in the car park, up and down past my window, with you running behind holding the saddle. I have put a little something for the children through your door. I hope your mother's house is warm and that M. likes having a garden. With love, Irena, 7C

units.title: Goodbye card for 11F
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Soraya and the kids moved out this morning to her mum's in Tollinby. They gave us notice a while ago and asked for no fuss, so this is the fuss: there's a card at Hassan's till for anyone who wants to sign it. I'll post it on Saturday. Please keep messages short and kind. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I signed at 20:40. I will miss R. asking every time if my van is the same van. It is always the same van. Sorry, my spelling on the card is bad, I wrote in capitals so it is clear.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Signed. For the record, and because I have seen the speculation elsewhere: 1. They gave notice weeks ago. 2. Soraya's mother has been unwell. 3. The transfer request predates most of what has been posted here. People are entitled to move without becoming evidence of anything.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Card is next to the till, under the lottery stand so it does not get chocolate on it. 23 names so far. Little M. came in with her grandmother this morning to buy a last lolly and said she was going to live 'where the stairs are outside'. I think she means a bungalow. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: not gonna make a joke about this one. M. used to wave at me through the gap in the lift doors every morning like i was a celebrity. building feels weird without the scooter noise on 11. signed it with a little drawing of a scooter which ivy will say is bad

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: It is bad (it looks like a toaster on a stick). I added a small drawing of the view from 11F with the canal and the gasholder, which R. once told me was 'the moon factory'. I've kept it in my sketchbook too, for no reason except that I liked the idea.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: signed it on my way in from the depot love, Hassan had the shutter half up and let me in, I wrote a bit long sorry Bev but I've known that girl since she was carrying R. in a sling up five flights when the lift was out that whole summer, she's a good one and I hope Tollinby knows it

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I signed the card this morning. I should like to say that it was a pleasure to see so many names on it. My husband used to say a building is only bricks until somebody leaves it, and then you find out who lived there. Irena, 7C

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: 41 signatures and three drawings, one of which Jordie insists is a scooter. Card goes in the post tomorrow. Thanks everyone. I'm leaving this thread open for a day and then I'll close it so it doesn't turn into anything else. Bev, DCRA

units.title: Thank you
units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Just a quick one from Tollinby. Thank you for the card, which Bev sent a photo of, and for the help with the van, and the sweets. R. has found a cat in the garden here and has named it Lift. M. slept through for the first time in weeks. I'll miss you all. Please look after Irena. S.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Lift is a brilliant name for a cat. Look after yourselves. Your post box key is with Hassan if anything turns up. Bev

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Two letters came today for 11F, I have them under the counter with the key. Tell R. the bike went to the boy on 4, he has already fixed the tyre with his dad. I will keep an eye on Irena, I see her every morning for the bread anyway. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: a cat called Lift is the funniest thing that has happened in this building all month and i'm including the time the lift alarm went off for an hour because of a pigeon. glad M. is sleeping. will carry irena's shopping, was already doing that, will keep doing that

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Soraya, thank you for your kind words. I do not need looking after, but I shall allow Jordie to carry my potatoes because it makes him feel useful. Please send me a drawing of the cat when R. has done one. You know my door. Irena, 7C

units.title: Stairwell 6-8 since the relay job: observations
units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Since the relay was replaced: 1. Lights on 6-8 have been continuously on for three nights (checked 21:00, 00:00, 06:00). 2. No flicker observed. 3. The push-button timers on 6 and 7 now do nothing, because the circuit is permanently live. 4. I have taken the stairs four times, 9 to ground. 5. Nothing to report. I am posting the nothing because nothing is also data.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good. This is the useful phase. With the flights lit, any future report can come with what you saw as well as what you heard, which removes most of the ambiguity. I'd expect reports to drop sharply now. Not because anything has gone, but because people can see the cough came from the bloke on 9 with the bin bag.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I still use the lift. I know the lights are on. I have read Tobin's list. I am not saying anything is there. I am saying I carry parcels all day and the lift is easier and I have decided. That is all.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: did the cardio of doom at 2am on purpose. lights blazing like a dentist's. 14 down to 6, then back up to 9 because i forgot my keys at tobin's (long story, chess). nothing. just me and my own trainers squeaking. honestly a bit disappointed lol. it's just stairs now

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, it is a great relief to have the light back. I walked down to Hassan's by the stairs yesterday morning for the first time in a fortnight and it was quite pleasant, if slow. My knees are another matter. I have nothing else to add today. Irena, 7C

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Notice ref KE/DC/0412. Kerrow Estates confirms that the replacement timer relay on the 6-8 riser was installed and tested by our approved contractor. The riser lighting will be monitored for fourteen days. Residents are asked to report any lighting fault through the repairs portal. We thank residents for their patience during this period.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Question for Kerrow, which I do not expect to be answered: 1. Is the circuit now permanently on by design, or is the timer function to be restored? 2. If permanently on, who pays for the electricity? 3. Will the push buttons be removed or labelled? Item 3 matters: two residents have told me they keep pressing them out of habit and assuming it worked.

units.author: relay_sparky
units.text: Answering since Kerrow won't. Popped in tonight on the way past. Lights on, staying on. I've wired it permanently live until they decide on the new timers, so the buttons do nothing for now; I'll stick labels on next visit. Electric is on the landlord's supply. Old relay's in my van if anyone wants to see what corroded contacts look like. Jem

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: jem i would genuinely like to see the corroded relay, i'm an engineering student, that's basically a museum piece to me. also thanks. it's nice walking up and being able to see the graffiti on 7 again. someone has drawn a very good duck

units.author: relay_sparky
units.text: Next time I'm in, knock on the riser door on 6, I'll show you. Fair warning, it's a grey box with green crust on it, not exactly a museum. The duck's been there since I first did a job here, years ago. Whoever drew it knew what they were doing. Jem

units.title: Not a stairwell post
units.author: dc_3_wendell

edit.text: I have said on this board that nothing happens on these stairs, and I still say that. Today at ten to twelve the lift was out, so I walked up to 3 with my shopping. Somebody was walking up the flight above me, step for step, and stopped when I stopped on the landing. Broad daylight, lights on. I went up to 4. Nobody. I will not be discussing it.

units.text: I have said on this board that nothing happens on these stairs, and I still say that. Today the lift was out, so I walked up to 3 with my shopping. Somebody was walking up the flight above me, step for step, and stopped when I stopped on the landing. Broad daylight, lights on. I went up to 4. Nobody. I will not be discussing it.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Housekeeping, and I mean this: Mr Pryce has asked not to be questioned about this, and I'm going to respect that. Please don't reply with theories aimed at him. If you've had a similar experience you're welcome to post your own. Bev, DCRA

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Not a theory aimed at anyone, just a general note, since Bev asked for none. In a reinforced concrete core, footfall from a flight two or three floors up can sound like it's on the flight directly above. Midday with the lift out is the busiest the stairs get. The 'stopped when I stopped' part is the bit I can't account for from here, and I won't pretend otherwise.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: I will not question Mr Pryce. I will only record, for my own purposes, that this is the first report I am aware of below floor 6, the first in full daylight, and the first since the relay was replaced. That is three firsts in one post. I have no further comment.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I was at work at midday, on the Mill Road route. I only say this so nobody thinks it was me on the stairs. I am glad you posted it, Mr Pryce. It is not easy to post a thing like this when you said the opposite before.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Lift's out, building full of people using the stairs at lunchtime, someone hears another person on the stairs. Lads. That's called living in a block of flats.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: cal you don't live here and the guy who posted this has spent three weeks calling the rest of us hysterical. if Mr Pryce says someone stopped when he stopped, i believe he heard it. anyway. thanks Mr Pryce. i'll stop now before bev locks it

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (I was asleep at noon, as is traditional.) I don't have a theory, only an observation: every report until now came from the dark. I'd quietly assumed the lights would fix it, the way you assume a nightmare stops when you open your eyes. I'm going to sit with that for a bit.

units.title: The roof door and my chair (14)
units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Small experiment (don't tell Bev). Last night at half two I put one of my kitchen chairs against the roof access door on 14, on the inside, legs touching the bar. This morning it was a metre away, facing the wall, neatly. The door was shut. I heard nothing, but I sleep with headphones. Drawing attached: the chair, from above, looking guilty.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ivy why would you do this to me at 2am. ok sensible questions: which way does the door open, and does the bar push out. because if it opens outward onto the roof the chair wouldn't stop anything, someone coming in from outside would just shove it. also ollie is going to be unbearable about this

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: It opens outward, push bar on my side. So yes, anyone coming in from the roof would have to pull it, and a chair against the bar wouldn't stop that or move. Which is why it's odd that it moved. (Unless someone on my side moved it, which is either a neighbour being tidy or a neighbour I'd like to meet less.)

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Ivy. I love you, but that's a fire exit, and you cannot put furniture in front of it, inside or out. If the fire brigade find a chair there, it's the association that gets the letter. Please don't repeat the experiment. Bev

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: The caretaker does a walk of the fire exits on some mornings very early, before six, he comes in for his paper after. He is a tidy man. I can ask him tomorrow if he moved a chair on 14. I would not be surprised. He once straightened my newspaper stand while I was serving. H

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Thank you Hassan, please do ask (and apologise to Bev on my behalf, I'm sorry Bev, the chair is back in my kitchen where it belongs). A tidy caretaker would honestly be the best possible answer. I'd buy him a paper myself. I'm not going to decide anything until he says.

units.title: Bin chute on 3 frozen shut
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The bin chute hatch on 3 is frozen shut, or something is jammed in it, and so people are leaving bags on the landing, which is a fire hazard and attracts the gulls through the broken window on the half-landing, which I reported in the spring. I have rung Kerrow twice. The menu has seven options and none of them is 'bins'.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Mr Pryce, I have a kettle and I am not afraid to use it. I poured warm water on the hatch on 3 at ten tonight and it opens now. Someone had jammed a pizza box in it sideways. I have taken the bags on the landing down to the big bins. Please do not put pizza boxes in the chute. H

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Thank you, Hassan. That is more than Kerrow has managed in eleven years. The pizza boxes come from 5, I would put money on it. I will be writing to the association about a sign. And about the gulls, again.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: oi Wendell I live on 5 and I've never ordered a pizza in my life love, I work nights and eat what the depot canteen hasn't burnt, it'll be the students on 6, no offence Jordie, but thanks Hassan for the kettle that's very good of you, I'd have just left it

units.title: Lift out again (fifth time)
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: The lift went down at about half eleven this morning and was back by four. Kerrow say the control board is 'under review' until the new year, which means it will break again. If you need help with shopping or getting up the stairs when it's out, post here or knock on 4A and I'll find someone. Bev

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: I carried for 7, 9 and 12 today. If the lift goes again, leave your bag at the shop with your flat number and I will bring it when I close. No charge, I am going up anyway, I live on 2, it is good for my heart, my doctor says. H

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: came home at five this morning love and the lift was fine then, it was after I'd gone to bed it went, so I've been lucky, the stairs are lit like a supermarket now anyway so I don't mind, though my knees do, anyone want a lift of soup I've made too much

units.title: Shop notice: cold weather
units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Cold weather this week. In the shop: de-icer, rock salt in small bags, candles, torches and batteries at cost price, hot water bottles. Bread comes at 06:15 now not 06:00 because the van is slow on the ice. If the power goes I have a gas ring and will do tea at the counter for anyone. H

units.author: dc_10_garrick
units.text: Legend, Hassan. Grabbed two bags of salt for the steps by the bike shed before my 6am client. Mate, those steps were a skating rink. If anyone wants a hand gritting the front path in the mornings I'm up at five anyway, just knock on 10C or shout.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Thank you Garrick. I have put a bucket of salt and a scoop by the front door with a sign saying 'for the path not for your car'. We will see how long it lasts. Also, I have more torches now. Someone bought eleven yesterday, I do not ask. H

units.title: Group session: night 6 log, and the last two nights
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Night 6 log. Five of us out, 22:30 to 04:00. Positions as before: me north ride (two omnis, dish), tern at the pumping house, odile on the car park bank with her binaural head, hollis at the dam, ned's loaned DAT on the east ride. Light wind until 01:00. Owls, a fox, a lorry on the Tollinby road at 02:12. Two knocks on my dish file at 02:38. Nothing on anyone else's. Two nights left. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so my file for night 6 has nothing at 02:38, which is weird because the pumping house is only 300 m off and I had the outflow running loud but not THAT loud. spectrogram attached, arrows on 02:36-02:40, honestly just water. clocks synced to network time at 22:30 and 04:00 (yes Hollis, both ends, I have screenshots).

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Noted on the clocks, and thanks for the screenshots. A 300 m path through woodland with water noise at the receiving end would easily bury a knock that's clear on a dish pointed the right way. Absence at the pumping house doesn't tell us much. Dunlin, which way was the dish pointing at 02:38?

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Northeast, toward the reservoir fence, same as every night. The dish isn't moving; I set it at 22:30 and leave it so I'm not handling it. So the knocks came from roughly that bearing, not from tern's side. I take the point about the water burying it. I'd still have expected odile's head to pick something up from the bank.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one: I've been through my night 6 file twice around 02:38 and there's a faint something, left and slightly behind the head, so northeast-ish. But after what I found in my own stairwell last week I'm not going to swear to direction. It's there, it's tiny, and I'm not localising it.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Your cars were in the reservoir car park until four again. Two nights left, you say. Fine. I'll be glad of it. The dam path is solid ice from tonight with this frost and if one of you goes in, nobody will hear you over your own microphones. Wear something bright and tell someone where you are.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear young man, I am glad the DAT is earning its keep. Do please keep it out of the frost when not in use; the tape can stick to the heads when cold and then you will hear a squeal and think it is a ghost. It is not a ghost, it is the pinch roller. Two knocks on one file sounds very like machinery at a distance to me. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Keeping this pinned until the session ends. Reminder for everyone following along: please listen to the raw files in the session folder, not the phone recordings of speakers that keep turning up in other places with music on them. And please respect the keeper's ask about the dam path.

units.title: Last night of the session: rota and frost kit
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Tonight's the last one. Same positions except hollis is staying home with a cold, so the dam is uncovered. Forecast minus six, calm. Practical: keep recorders inside your jacket until deployment, lithium batteries only, and bring a flask. Everyone check in on the group chat at the top of each hour. If you miss two check-ins I'll come and find you.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I'm in, thermal socks, two pairs, plus the binaural head odile lent me again (I will guard it with my life). quick q: do we want the dam covered? I could move over from the pumping house. or is it better to keep me where I've been every night so the comparison holds

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Stay at the pumping house. Same place every night is the whole point, otherwise we're just people with microphones wandering about. Leave the dam empty. Thanks for checking. See you in the car park at half ten.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Sorry to drop out on the last night. Annoyingly this is the best acoustic night of the lot: no wind, cold dense air, sound will carry a long way along the ground. Expect frost cracks from the trees and the ice; they're sharp, broadband and can be mistaken for knocks. Log them anyway and we'll sort them later.

units.title: Brackwater group session: wrap-up
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: That's the session done. Eight nights, up to six recordists, roughly 180 hours of audio, all in the session folder and now catalogued. Totals: knocks on my dish on four nights; two of those also faintly on odile's head; none elsewhere. One disputed sound on tern's night 3 file. Last night: frost cracks, owls, nothing else. Thank you all. No theory, just the files.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so huge thanks to dunlin for organising, seriously. and I know everyone's tired of the night 3 thing but I still can't make it be anything I know. I've tried fox, heron, deer, a gate, someone on the road. it's 1.4 seconds and it goes up at the end. that's all. sorry, I'll stop. (typo fixed: 1.4 not 4.1)

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Don't apologise. I said last week it isn't water hammer and I stand by that; the spectrum is wrong. A heron's call at a few hundred metres in damp air is my best guess, but I've listened to forty heron clips and none of them goes up at the end like yours. So: unidentified. That's an honest answer and it's allowed.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Thank you dunlin, best fortnight of recording I've had in years, frozen toes and all. Tern, the head is yours as long as you need it. For the record: my two faint knocks are real events on the file, but I'm no longer claiming direction for anything in that wood after my stairwell experiment. Reflections are slippery.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: All session files are now in the catalogue as LB-1104 to LB-1131 with your location notes and kit lists. Where clocks disagreed I've recorded both times rather than choose. Listening notes are mine and neutral. If I've misspelt your kit, tell me and I'll correct it. Thank you for the cleanest metadata this archive has ever received.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Unpinning the nightly logs and pinning this instead. This is what LowBand is for: recordings, metadata, people disagreeing politely about spectra. Well done everyone. If you want to keep discussing individual files, start a thread per file so it doesn't turn into one long argument.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thanks odile. I might go back out on my own some nights, just the dish, quietly, now the crowd's gone. Not for any reason except that four nights out of eight is too many to just stop. Keeper, if you're reading, I'll park on the lane, not in your car park.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Parking on the lane makes no difference to me, lad, it's you in the woods I mind, not your car. If you must go, go when there's a moon and tell somebody where you are. And keep off the dam.

units.title: Gilliver harbour mouth, 2 h hydrophone: a hum I can't place
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Dropped the hydrophone off Bram's boat at the harbour mouth last night, 22:50 to 00:50. Raw file in the folder. Expected: hull slap, a prop or two, the ice plant pump. Got those, plus a low hum, around 50 Hz with harmonics, that runs about twelve minutes, stops for eight, starts again. Like a fridge compressor. Nothing on that harbour cycles like that. Annoying.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Twelve on, eight off is textbook thermostat cycling. A refrigerated unit on a moored boat with shore power, or a chest freezer in a harbourside shed, would do it. Water carries low frequencies a very long way and the source needn't be anywhere near the mic. I'd look along the quay before I looked anywhere else.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: That was my first thought. But the harbour was dark from 23:10, the coast road cut, so anything on shore power was off. Ice plant was off. I'm a marine fitter; I know which boats have gensets and none were running. The hum carried on straight through the cut. So it's on its own supply, or it's not where I think.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I ran your file through the same settings as my session stuff and the hum is really clean, like suspiciously clean, almost no drift in pitch. spectrogram attached with the on and off times marked. 00:02 to 00:14 on, 00:14 to 00:22 off, etc. whatever it is it's very regular.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Battery-backed things that cycle: emergency lighting chargers, a boat's own fridge on a battery bank, a refrigerated lorry on its own diesel parked by the slip. Was there anything parked on the harbour road? A reefer trailer would be loud but very steady.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Good thought. Asked Rook at the chandlery, who sees everything. No lorries on the harbour road that night. Two boats with battery fridges, both owners say switched off. I'll walk the quay with a handheld tonight and see if I can find it in air. It's a pump somewhere. It's always a pump.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Listened with good headphones. It's a lovely clean recording, Marlo, and I agree it sounds like a fridge, the exact noise my kitchen makes at night when I'm trying to sleep. Underwater I can't tell you a thing about direction. Good luck with the quay walk.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear Marlo, I once spent a week hunting a hum on a tape that turned out to be the mains transformer in my own recorder, picked up through the case. Has your hydrophone amplifier got its own battery, and might it be charging something? I only ask because it took me a week. Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Fair question, Ned. Amp's on a sealed lead-acid, no charger in the loop. Ran it into a dummy load in my workshop this afternoon for two hours: nothing at 50 Hz. So it's in the water. Walked the quay at nine with the handheld. Cold, quiet, nothing cycling in air. Will try again.

units.title: Dellow Court riser, post-repair: three nights of nothing
units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Cross-posting for completeness. With the lights now on, I left a handheld recorder on the 7th-floor landing for three nights, 23:00 to 03:00. Results: n=3 nights, 12 hours. Footfall events: 9, each matched to a resident I saw or heard arrive. Unmatched events: 0. Door closures: 31. I offer this without conclusion.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Thank you. This is exactly the kind of baseline that was missing. I'd note, gently, that the lights changing behaviour changes what's measured: people use the stairs more when they're lit, which is part of why your matched count is high. But zero unmatched in twelve hours is a clean result.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you Tobin. I am glad it is quiet. For the old recording, I still say the same: there is no fridge on floor 8 that I know of. But this is good. I am happy to have a boring stairwell. I have also learned the word baseline.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Leaving this open since it's raw data and nicely presented. Please keep the stairwell discussion here to the recordings themselves; the building's own board is the place for anything about residents.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Addendum. My recorder was on 7, at night. A resident has today reported an event on 3, at midday, which my method could not have captured. I am not drawing a conclusion from that either. I am only noting the limit of three nights on one landing. Method has edges.

units.title: What a hard frost sounds like (for anyone confusing it with knocks)
units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Since everyone's going to be out in this calm cold spell: frost cracks are sharp, very short, and they come from all around you, low and to the sides, from the ground and the tree trunks. They don't repeat in a pattern. Headphones on for my clip from the park last night: you can hear them pop under the grass like someone stepping on bubble wrap far away.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Useful, thank you. That matches my last-night file: dozens of cracks from 23:00, random spacing, all around the omnis. None of them like the evenly spaced knocks on the earlier nights. Worth having on record that the wood can make a racket on its own in a frost.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Same on the water: thin ice forming in the inner harbour last night ticks and sings underwater, quite high, almost metallic. Thought my cable was faulty for ten minutes. If anyone hears whale song off Gilliver this week, it's the slip freezing.

units.title: A reel from the Lisle ferry, 1971
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear all, a friend's widow passed me a box of reels, and one is labelled 'Lisle boat, night, 1971'. It is a lovely thing: the old ferry's diesel, the bell, men talking about the price of beer, and gulls. I have digitised it at 7.5 inches per second and put it in the folder. There is print-through at the start, which is an echo of the next layer of tape, not a ghost. Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: That's the old Lisle Lass, I'd put money on it. Twin-cylinder, you can hear the slight miss on the second. My dad worked on her. Thanks Ned, that's a proper bit of history. The bell's the one they took off when she was scrapped, it's in the Gilliver chapel now.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: How marvellous, thank you. I shall add the name to my notes and pass it to the catalogue keeper. I did wonder about the miss; I thought it might be the tape. It is a pleasant thing when the machine is innocent for once. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Received, thank you both. I'll catalogue it with the vessel name marked as 'identified by a listener' rather than confirmed, as usual. It's a lovely clean transfer. I'd be glad of the label photographed too, front and back; sometimes there's a date pencilled in that nobody notices.
